Workflow and composite actions pinned by tag, not by commit SHA, across a large CI tree. Supply-chain hardening, not a vulnerability.

70 hits are the Arabic UI locale (webui i18n/locales/ar.ts); the rest are RTL test strings and the link-policy / notification code that handles bidi controls. Legitimate right-to-left text, not hidden source.

Electron main-process packaging and installer services (agent-seeder, after-pack, appimage-launcher, backend-installer). Spot-checked: joins of readdir entry names and install-directory constants, with no renderer or network input.
Installer smoke tests, release utilities and the embedded Lemonade client calling configured local endpoints; most hits are under util/ and installer/.
SQLite memory store, UI database and scratchpad: f-strings carry fixed table names (FTS5 'optimize') and PRAGMA values from code, while data values are bound parameters.
Same call sites as the raw-query rule: identifiers and PRAGMAs from code, values bound.
Regexes built from app-side constants and escaped search terms in the web UI; no ReDoS-shaped user pattern found in the spot check.
The Go TUI launches the GAIA agent and its helpers; that is what it is for. Program paths are resolved by the TUI, with no shell.

Every interpolation is a maintainer-controlled input (workflow_dispatch / workflow_call / composite-action inputs) or a static matrix value; none comes from a pull_request_target or issue_comment event field.
CI installs tools from their vendors with curl | sh. Supply-chain hardening item.
Log lines use 'token' / 'credential' / 'secret' as nouns (credential reads, skill budgets, Discord credentials file) without logging the value.
Python 3.6 compatibility rule; the project requires a modern Python.
Python 3.6 compatibility rule; the project requires a modern Python.
Electron services and npm lifecycle scripts starting the GAIA backend and installers with argv arrays.
Reusable first-party workflows called with secrets: inherit from the same repository.
Agent and provider factories importing from an internal registry, plus two lint utilities.
Five are the project's own chmod 0o700 on private state directories (connectors, daemon, attempts); one is 0o755 on a lock queue directory. Loosening per the rule's advice would weaken them.
Loopback-only Electron servers; the browser-pane bridge requires a bearer token from a user-only discovery file.
python_runner.py is the agent's Python execution tool (product surface); frozen.py runs the bundled entry script in a frozen build.
SHA-1 used as a content fingerprint or cache key, not for authentication.
TUI control server: loopback-only, bearer token required, plain-text responses.
Test and visual-regression files.

Service-worker unit test writing a static index.html fixture.
util/verify_publish_pipeline.py evaluates a parsed ast.Expression from the repo's own workflow file; release tooling.
globals().get('anthropic') checks for a lazily imported module.
Performance rule, not security.

records.rule: docs/package-lock.json (proxy-addr, qs, body-parser, path-to-regexp, follow-redirects, picomatch)
records.detail: Small Express auth proxy in front of the hosted docs. The proxy-addr Critical concerns a trusted-subnet list matched against IPv4-mapped IPv6; server.js sets trust proxy to a hop count (1), not a subnet list. The rest are dependency currency. Not examined further: it fronts a live deployment.
Indirect x/net v0.38.0 and x/text v0.30.0 in the TUI and its vendored bubbletea; the TUI parses no untrusted HTML and runs no HTTP/2 server. Bump for currency.
js-yaml DoS CVEs in the web UI build tree; YAML inputs are first-party.
Docs, build, test-fixture and agent-hub worker Dockerfiles; none is the desktop product.

Hand review; no tool rule covers it. One first-party finding (High proposed), reported privately through GitHub private vulnerability reporting on 2026-11-28, as SECURITY.md asks. Detail withheld until a fix ships.
